sections.heading: Algebraic comparisons at a fixed value

questions.q: Given $x=5$. Column A: $2x+3$. Column B: $x+8$. Compare the two columns.
Given $x=4$. Column A: $(x+2)^2$. Column B: $x^2+4x+4$. Compare the two columns.
questions.answer: $(x+2)^2$ expands to $x^2+4x+4$ for every value of $x$, so the columns are always equal. $A=B$.

questions.q: Given $n=-2$. Column A: $n^2$. Column B: $n^3$. Compare the two columns.
Given $x=3$. Column A: $5x-2$. Column B: $2(x+5)$. Compare the two columns.
For any real number $x$: Column A: $x$. Column B: $x^2$. Compare the two columns.
questions.answer: If $x=2$: $B>A$. If $x=\dfrac{1}{2}$: $A>B$. If $x=1$: $A=B$. The relationship changes, so it cannot be determined.

questions.q: For any real number $x$: Column A: $x+5$. Column B: $2x$. Compare the two columns.
questions.answer: If $x=5$: $A=B$. If $x=0$: $A>B$. If $x=10$: $B>A$. The relationship changes, so it cannot be determined.

questions.q: For any real number $x$: Column A: $|x|$. Column B: $x$. Compare the two columns.
questions.answer: If $x\geq0$: $A=B$. If $x<0$ (e.g. $x=-3$): $A=3$, $B=-3$, so $A>B$. Since the relationship is not the same in every case, it cannot be determined.

questions.q: Given only that $n$ is an integer: Column A: $n^2$. Column B: $4$. Compare the two columns.
questions.answer: If $n=1$: $A=1<4$. If $n=3$: $A=9>4$. The relationship changes, so it cannot be determined.

questions.q: For any real number $x$: Column A: $(x-3)^2$. Column B: $x^2-6x+9$. Compare the two columns.
questions.answer: Expanding: $(x-3)^2=x^2-6x+9$ for every value of $x$, so the columns are always equal. $A=B$.

questions.q: Column A: the perimeter of a square with side $6$ cm. Column B: the perimeter of a rectangle with length $8$ cm and width $3$ cm. Compare the two columns.
Column A: the area of a circle with radius $4$ cm (use $\pi\approx3.14$). Column B: the area of a square with side $7$ cm. Compare the two columns.
Column A: the sum of the interior angles of a pentagon. Column B: the sum of the interior angles of two triangles. Compare the two columns.
Column A: the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs $5$ and $12$. Column B: $14$. Compare the two columns.
Column A: the value of $x$, if $x:12=3:4$. Column B: $10$. Compare the two columns.
A recipe uses flour and sugar in the ratio $3:1$. Column A: the sugar needed for $240$ g of flour. Column B: $90$ g. Compare the two columns.
Column A: the sum of the parts in the simplified form of the ratio $18:24$. Column B: $8$. Compare the two columns.
questions.answer: $18:24$ simplifies to $3:4$, so the sum of parts is $3+4=7$. $B=8$. $B>A$.

questions.q: Two numbers are in the ratio $5:3$, and their sum is $96$. Column A: the larger number. Column B: $61$. Compare the two columns.
questions.answer: Total parts $=5+3=8$, each part $=12$. Larger number $=5\times12=60$. $B=61$. $B>A$.

questions.q: A data set is $4,7,7,9,13$. Column A: the mean. Column B: the median. Compare the two columns.
Column A: the range of the data set $3,8,15,22$. Column B: $20$. Compare the two columns.
A bag contains 3 red balls and 5 blue balls. Column A: the probability of drawing a red ball. Column B: the probability of drawing a blue ball. Compare the two columns.
Column A: the total cost of 4 items at 15 riyals each, after a $10\%$ discount on the total. Column B: $55$ riyals. Compare the two columns.
questions.answer: Total before discount $=4\times15=60$ riyals. After discount: $60\times0.9=54$ riyals. $B=55$. $B>A$.

questions.q: Ali's age is $3$ years more than twice Sara's age. Sara is $8$. Column A: Ali's age. Column B: $20$. Compare the two columns.
Column A: the simple interest earned on 2,000 riyals at $5\%$ per year for 3 years. Column B: $350$ riyals. Compare the two columns.
A car travels 240 km using 20 liters of fuel. Column A: the distance travelled per liter. Column B: $12$ km per liter. Compare the two columns.
Given that $5<x<9$. Column A: $x$. Column B: $7$. Compare the two columns.
questions.answer: If $x=6$: $A<B$. If $x=8$: $A>B$. The relationship changes, so it cannot be determined.

questions.q: Given that $x>10$. Column A: $x$. Column B: $10$. Compare the two columns.
questions.answer: Since $x$ is always greater than $10$, $A>B$ in every case.

questions.q: Given that $0<x<1$. Column A: $x$. Column B: $x^2$. Compare the two columns.
questions.answer: For any value strictly between $0$ and $1$ (e.g. $x=0.5$: $x^2=0.25<0.5$), squaring makes the value smaller. $A>B$ in every case.

questions.q: Given that $-5\leq x\leq-1$. Column A: $x^2$. Column B: $10$. Compare the two columns.
questions.answer: If $x=-1$: $A=1<10$. If $x=-5$: $A=25>10$. The relationship changes, so it cannot be determined.
